question: The Tisza Party’s parliamentary majority has adopted a legislative package which, according to the Hungarian Government, was necessary for Hungary to unlock EU funds currently being withheld.

The law repeals Section 1(c) and Subtitle 16/A of Act CLI of 2011, which empowered the Constitutional Court to issue preliminary interpretative opinions under the Fundamental Law on Hungary’s constitutional order, sovereignty, national identity, constitutional traditions and fundamental rights.

During a session of the Hungarian Parliament’s Committee on European Affairs, the Parliamentary State Secretary for Justice stated that all amendments in the package resulted from consultations with the Commission. Given that this repeal directly affects Hungary’s constitutional order, while its link to the protection of the EU’s financial interests remains unclear: 1.

Did the Commission, during negotiations with the new Hungarian Government, request the repeal of Section 1(c) and Subtitle 16/A of Act CLI of 2011, or make the disbursement of EU funds conditional, in any way, on such a repeal?

If it did, what is the legal basis in EU law for such a request and what is the direct link between this requirement, the protection of the EU’s financial interests and the conditions for access to EU funds?
If not, how does the Commission assess the Hungarian Government’s claim?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.9.2026) In the spirit of sincere cooperation, the Commission has exchanged with the Hungarian government. The technical discussions concerned open issues in various domains, including procedures to protect the EU’s financial interests from rule of law breaches and corruption risks.

As announced on 29 May 20261, the Commission and the Hungarian authorities agreed on a robust architecture to ensure that Hungary addresses corruption and rule of law concerns to access Union funding currently on hold under different procedures. The Hungarian government is treating the reforms needed as a top priority.

It is for Hungary to submit (i) a written notification under the Conditionality Regulation2, (ii) a first payment request under the Resilience and Recovery Fund Regulation3 and (iii) its positive self-assessment on the fulfilment of the Charter horizontal enabling condition of the Common Provisions Regulation4, for the Commission to assess the reforms under the respective legal frameworks and, in the case of the Conditionality procedure, the Council to lift the measures.
The Commission does not comment on Member States’ internal legislative processes or negotiations, including the dialogue between the government and the parliament.
